items.title: Eardrum damaged after assault: Kerala activist recounts Delhi Police violence
items.summary: Fidal Royas, a member of the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) from Kerala, said the Delhi Police detained him five times between October 2 and October 11. Each day, after being released, Fidal and his comrades returned to the Communist Party of India (Marxist) head office in HKS Surjeet Bhavan, where they were staying, only to return the next day to the protest site. But on October 11, he was brutally assaulted, leading to a ‘traumatic perforation’ of his eardrum. A native of Kuttiyadi in Kozhikode district, Fidal was among 30-odd DYFI and Students Federation of India (SFI) activists from Kerala who travelled to Delhi on October 1, with the aim of participating in the protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Speaking to TNM , he recounted the events of October 11. Left student and youth organisations took out a march from Rajiv Chowk Metro Station towards Janpath that afternoon. “That day, the demonstration was declared suddenly. We went to Rajiv Chowk between 12 noon and 12.30 pm to take part in it.” Fidal said that he was at the rear end of the march when police started detaining protesters from the back. “I was among the first to be detained and taken into a police bus, the kind with cells. Then others were also detained in the bus, which started moving. Some of us started recording videos from within the bus. The police objected to this and started assaulting us,” he recalled. According to Fidal, one of the cops in the bus stepped out and told five or six others that he had recorded videos. “The cops then proceeded to assault me severely. They put me on the road and beat me with bare hands and kicked me with their boots as I lay on the road. They repeatedly assaulted me, even slapping me on my face till my body couldn’t take it anymore. One after the other, they kept beating me.” “I was beaten continuously for at least five minutes,” Fidal continued, adding that his ear started hurting then. “I was in a lot of pain initially,” he said. The assault continued even after Fidal was put in a second bus, he alleged. “The cops kept assaulting the detainees in that bus also. items.title: Mini Cooper crash: Kerala court denies bail to accused Suhail Sajeev and 3 others
items.summary: A Kerala court on Saturday denied bail to Suhail Sajeev and three others, booked in connection with the Mini Cooper car accident which led to the death of three motorcyclists. Sajeev along with Ninav, Joel and Ameer had filed bail applications before a trial court in Angamaly. However, Judicial First Class Magistrate Samyuktha MK dismissed their bail pleas. The case stemmed from an accident which happened on October 11 when a Mini Cooper driven by Sajeev at high speed hit a scooter carrying three youngsters on the Athani-Airport Road in Nedumbassery, killing all three. According to the First Information Report (FIR), the impact threw all three onto the road, causing severe injuries to their heads and bodies. While two of them died on the spot, the third succumbed to injuries later. The Nedumbassery Airport Police Station registered a case under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The police subsequently arrested Sajeev and three others in connection with the incident. The three were riding in the car along with Sajeev, who was behind the wheel. All four accused were remanded to 14 days of judicial custody on October 14. According to reports , Sajeev was driving under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. During the bail hearing on October 16, the counsel appearing for the accused argued that the incident only amounted to rash and negligent driving rather than culpable homicide. It was also argued that the victims too had violated the traffic rules as all three of them were riding on a scooter while using the middle lane of the road. The abetment charges against the other three accused were challenged on the ground that they had only accompanied Sajeev in the car. However, the prosecution and the victim's counsel opposed the bail plea, arguing that the accident could not be treated as an ordinary case of negligent driving. CCTV footage was relied upon to show that all the accused had visited several bars and were inebriated before the accident. It was also alleged that the co-accused in the car had encouraged Sajeev to drive, despite knowing that he was drunk. The Court today dismissed the bail pleas. Advocates Saiby Jose Kidangoor, Sreeraj S Rajaram and Afsana Khan appeared for Sajeev.

items.title: Another rape, another suo motu cognizance, but what happens after?
items.summary: Recently, the Supreme Court, in a suo motu writ petition In Re: Recent rape incidents in Delhi NCR gave directions on institutional reforms for improving women’s safety in the Delhi-NCR region. The Court’s intervention comes in the aftermath of the alleged gang-rape of a 17-year old minor in Delhi’s Aastha Kunj Park. This is not the first instance the Court has taken suo motu cognizance of a matter concerning women’s safety against sexual violence. In 2024, the Court did the same in the RG Kar case and gave directions for the creation of safer working conditions for medical professionals. While such initiatives from the Court are admirable, a harder question to answer is: what happens after such directions are issued? The Court’s directions, without any corresponding enforcement mechanism, fail to achieve the aim that they are issued with. The suo motu cognizance addresses institutional failure as a common denominator in such instances of crimes against women. Pointing to the same, the Court also commented on how solidarity shown by the authorities is not the answer to this “ social evil ”. The Court’s order accounts for existing preventive measures like the National Database on Sexual Offenders, the Safe City Project and One Stop Centres. It tries to assess their demonstrated efficacy in fulfilling their purpose. In its subsequent order on October 5 , the Court also directed the Delhi Police to set up real-time monitoring cells in addition to CCTV surveillance in public spaces. The two orders by the Court demonstrate a vigorous attack on institutional failure. However, this vigour is bound to fizzle down without attached subsequent action, which is what happened in the 2024 case. In August 2024 , the Court took suo motu cognizance in the case of the rape and murder of a trainee doctor in RG Kar Medical College and proposed the constitution of a National Task Force (NTF). The NTF was tasked with formulating recommendations for enhanced safety and better working conditions for medical professionals. In November 2024 , the NTF submitted its recommendations for better working conditions and prevention of violence (including sexual violence) against medical professionals. In December 2025 , this suo motu petition was closed by the Supreme Court and the matter was transferred back to the Calcutta High Court. items.title: PIL in Calcutta High Court seeks double-side printing on A4 paper for pleadings in West Bengal courts
items.summary: A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) has been filed before the Calcutta High Court seeking a uniform mandate for filing physical pleadings and documents in 75 GSM A4 paper in duplex (back-to-back) format in the High Court and other courts across West Bengal [Akash Sharma v. Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta and Another] . The PIL aims to lower paper consumption, printing services and costs and the physical bulk of court records. The case is listed for hearing on November 23. Calcutta High Court on February 22, 2021 had asked its administrative side to consider mandating use of A4 paper with double-side printing for pleadings and filings. However, the plea filed by advocate Akash Sharma states that further progress of the matter could not be ascertained through publicly available records or notices. This PIL primarily seeks to determine the outcome of the order dated February 22, 2021 and a fresh consideration of the matter to prescribe a uniform practice of using 75 GSM A4 paper in a duplex-printed format across all courts in the State.

items.title: Delhi SEM court grants bail to CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke
items.summary: A Delhi court on Saturday granted bail to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. The order was passed by a court of the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM). Dipke's legal team confirmed the development. The Court has imposed certain conditions on him. Details are awaited. Dipke and All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora were detained by the Delhi Police on October 16 ahead of the ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest at Connaught Place. Dipke was picked up near his residence while heading to the protest at Connaught Place while Bora was detained while she was marching from Mandi House. Notably, CJP activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are already in judicial custody after they tried to enter Jantar Mantar area.

items.title: Alliance Air pays over ₹16 lakh to 33 passengers after consumer court issues NBW over flight cancellation
items.summary: Over two years after abruptly cancelling a Hyderabad–Mysore flight, Alliance Air has cleared more than ₹16 lakh in compensation to 33 passengers following the issuance of non-bailable warrants by a Hyderabad consumer commission [Radha Devi Mandhana vs M/s The Alliance Aviation Ltd]. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-II, Hyderabad, comprising President Vakkanti Narasimha Rao and Members P V T R Jawahar Babu and Suma Vala , terminated execution proceedings on October 14 after recording satisfaction of the decree. The Bench also recalled the non-bailable warrants (NBWs) previously issued against airline officials. The dispute arose from an incident on June 2, 2022, when a 33-member family group, including senior citizens and infants, arrived at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport to board a flight to Mysore. Less than three hours before departure, the airline sent an SMS notifying them of the flight's cancellation. Left stranded without assistance or refreshments, the passengers were offered alternate seats only for a few members of the group, which they could not take. Alliance Air then issued a written communication advising them to cancel their trip entirely. The cancellation resulted in a forfeiture of ₹2.70 lakh spent on non-refundable hotel stays in Ooty and Mudumalai, alongside pre-booked cab rentals. By an order dated July 11, 2024, the Commission held Alliance Air guilty of gross deficiency in service and non-compliance with Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) passenger care norms. The carrier was directed to pay ₹2.70 lakh towards actual financial losses, ₹9.90 lakh in aggregate compensation (₹30,000 per passenger), and ₹20,000 in litigation costs within 45 days, failing which the awarded amount would attract 12% annual interest. The complaint against Air India was dismissed as it was a distinct corporate entity after its privatisation. When the airline failed to satisfy the award, the consumers filed an execution plea. On August 25 this year, the Commission dismissed the airline’s Section 317 CrPC application seeking exemption from personal appearance, observed continued non-compliance and issued NBWs against the airline. Following the coercive order, the carrier delivered a demand draft covering the entire decretal sum along with accrued default interest, taking the total payout past ₹16 lakh. items.title: Democracy must allow its citizens to question the government: CM DK Shivakumar at NLSIU
items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday said that a strong democracy is not one where everyone agrees with the government but one which allows its citizens to question the government. At a time when democratic institutions across the world are facing challenges, young lawyers and policymakers have a special responsibility to protect the Constitution and uphold democratic values, he opined. “A strong democracy must allow its citizens to question the government. A strong democracy is not one where everyone agrees with the government. It is one where every citizen has the freedom to question the government. Never stop questioning, never compromise on your values and never forget the people,” he said. Shivakumar was addressing graduating students at the 34th convocation ceremony of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) at the Jnana Jyothi Auditorium in Bengaluru. He urged law graduates to question, debate and challenge ideas while also taking responsibility for finding solutions. Constitutional principles, he said, must not remain confined to textbooks but should guide governance, policymaking and public life. “India does not merely need more lawyers. We need lawyers with integrity, compassion and courage. You must understand the struggles of ordinary people and speak up for what is right, however difficult it may be,” he told the graduates. The CM also announced that the Karnataka government would establish a dedicated institution to train law graduates for judicial services examinations and provide continuing education to young lawyers. The government would also support the establishment of a start-up law clinic at NLSIU, where students, faculty members and lawyers would offer pro bono legal advice to young entrepreneurs, he said. Shivakumar also flagged the issue of pendency in courts and highlighted that crores of cases remain pending before Indian courts, leaving individuals and families waiting for justice. “What may be just another case number for us could be someone's entire life. It is essential to make justice faster, simpler, affordable and accessible to everyone,” he said. He said India's goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047 should not be measured merely through economic growth, infrastructure and employment, but also through the dignity, liberty, equality and security enjoyed by its citizens. items.title: Delhi High Court allows Britannia to use ‘no added sugar, no maida, no palm oil’ claim on biscuit packs
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday stayed an order passed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) restraining Britannia from mentioning 'no added sugar', 'no maida' and 'no palm oil' on the packaging and advertisements of its NutriChoice Millets Cookies. Justice Amit Mahajan said that these claims cannot be alleged to be an advertisement undermining the product of other manufacturers or influence the consumers’ behaviour in violation of the regulations. The Court also noted that Britannia has already agreed to manufacture the product without the claim “100% millets”. “The impugned order dated 09.10.2026, is stayed. The petitioner, as noted above, can produce and market its product, however, without the claim “100% Millets”,” the Court said. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court Justice Mahajan passed the order while dealing with a plea filed by Britannia against the FSSAI order asking it to remove claims regarding no added sugar, maida or palm oil. Britannia argued that the directions are based on an incorrect factual premise and were issued without a reasoned decision. It contended that it never committed to withdrawing the three claims during a personal hearing on October 7. It argued that “no maida” and “no palm oil” are factual statements about the ingredients used in the product and are not prohibited under the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018. Britannia also said that FSSAI circulated the September notice to licensing authorities, e-commerce platforms and social media platforms, seeking legal action and removal of advertisements before the company was even heard. Senior Advocate Sandeep Sethi with advocates Rajesh Batra, Sonia Kukreja, Rohit Chandra, Dhruba Dhar, Sadhika Kochhar, Krisna Gambhir and Shreya Sethi appeared for Britannia. [Read Order]

items.title: Delhi High Court imposes costs of ₹1 on Niva Bupa for misusing IP jurisdiction to sue influencer
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently imposed nominal costs of ₹1 on Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited for misusing its Intellectual Property (IP) Division's jurisdiction to sue a social media influencer over posts against the insurance company [Niva Bupa Vs Vishal Rattewal]. Justice Anup J Bhambhani held that merely referring to a company's trademark while criticising its services does not constitute trademark infringement, particularly when the person making such statements is not using the mark in the course of trade. "Since the suit was filed and pressed, this court is of the view that filing of such suit amounts to misuse of the special jurisdiction of this court under the Intellectual Property Division, " the Court observed. Anup Jairam Bhambhani The case arose from a lawsuit filed by Niva Bupa and an advocate representing the company (plaintiffs) against social media influencer Vishal Rattewal. They sought removal of the content published on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and X, besides an apology, damages of ₹5 crore and litigation costs. The dispute originated from a consumer complaint filed by Neeraj Kumar concerning a medical insurance claim against Niva Bupa. On October 9, 2024, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission at Charkhi Dadri in Haryana ruled in favour of Kumar and made certain observations concerning medical insurance companies generally. Niva Bupa alleged that Rattewal subsequently published offensive material about the company based on these proceedings. The insurer also objected to his references to an August 2026 order of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), which barred Niva Bupa from opening new places of business for six months over regulatory violations. Niva Bupa argued that Rattewal was attracting social media engagement by disparaging its services and damaging its reputation and infringing its registered trademark. However, the Court questioned how such allegations constituted trademark infringement under the Trade Marks Act, 1999. It noted that Rattewal was neither engaged in the insurance business nor connected with it. The Court held that merely using a company's name to identify it in allegedly disparaging posts did not constitute use of its trademark in the course of trade. Consequently, the Court concluded that the dispute did not involve infringement of intellectual property rights and could not be entertained by its IP Division. items.title: Delhi High Court quashes SFIO probe into Educomp Solutions
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has quashed the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) investigation into the affairs of education technology company Educomp Solutions Limited [Vinod Kumar Dandona v Union of India & Ors] . In an order dated October 16, Justice Amit Mahajan held that the Central government’s order of August 17, 2018, directing the probe was passed mechanically and without application of mind. “The cavalier manner in which the material, as noted above, has been cited, for justifying the entrusting of the investigation to the SFIO, in the opinion of this Court, ought to be deprecated,” the Court said. It added that the officers appointed under the Companies Act are experts in matters of corporate governance, and they cannot rely upon unsubstantiated material and reports to justify serious action as contemplated under Section 212(1)(c) of the Companies Act. Section 212(1)(c) empowers the Central Government to order an investigation into the affairs of a company by the SFIO. Justice Amit Mahajan Justice Mahajan passed the order while hearing petitions filed by Educomp’s former independent director Vinod Kumar Dandona, founder Shantanu Prakash, director Jagdish Prakash, Learning Leadership Foundation and former chief financial officer Ashish Mittal. The SFIO probe concerned allegations of financial irregularities, including account manipulation, diversion of funds, fictitious transactions and undervalued sale of group companies. The petitioners argued that the investigation was ordered without sufficient material and that earlier inspections had not established fraud or diversion of funds. They also alleged that the probe stemmed from a corporate rivalry involving former business partner Raffles Group. However, the Central government defended its decision. It stated that it followed a June 2018 oversight committee review of inspection reports, lenders’ complaints, references from the Prime Minister’s Office and media reports. The Court also examined an article published by The Wire, which was among the material relied upon to justify the probe. Justice Mahajan held that a newspaper report, without independent corroboration, could not by itself, justify an SFIO investigation. The inspection reports had not found evidence of siphoning or defalcation of funds. A letter from a Member of Parliament was also insufficient to justify the probe, the Court said. items.title: Only ground for transfer of matrimonial case to a different court is convenience of weaker party: Gujarat High Court
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court recently observed that courts must lean toward targeted affirmative action to ensure women have equal access to justice in matrimonial proceedings [Purvaben vs Hirenbhai Chaganbhai Solanki] . Justice D N Ray added that women deserve to be protected so that their right to legal remedy does not become illusory due to the inherent difficulties they face while in litigation. "The only test is to be applied is the convenience of the weaker party. While suppression, misdeclaration etc., on the part of the applicant would always have their due weightage before any court of law, the primary ingredient which would influence the decision of the Court would be whether, by transferring a petition from one jurisdiction to the other, the Court has been able to balance the inherent inequality which the party seeking access to legal remedy is faced with," the Court said. Justice D N Ray The Court added that matrimonial disputes represent a distinct category of litigation where parties often suffer more through the legal process than the grievance itself. "Matrimonial disputes form a special category of disputes where both the parties suffer through the process of litigation sometimes even more than the malady they were seeking to redress by invoking legal remedies available to them. The legal process very often itself becomes the punishment," the Court said. The Court was dealing an application filed by a wife under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), seeking the transfer of a family suit from the family court at Amreli to the family Court at Junagadh, situated roughly 100 kilometers away. The applicant submitted that she has no independent source of income and finds it exceedingly difficult to bear travel expenses and legal fees to attend the proceedings at Amreli. The husband opposed the plea and sought its dismissal. Invoking Article 15(3) of the Constitution, the Court emphasized that the judiciary must move past formal non-discrimination to foster substantive social justice. "Protective discrimination is a tool of social context judging by which two inherently inequal parties accessing legal remedies are deliberately discriminated upon, so that thereafter, they have equal access to the legal remedy," the Court observed. It underlined that at the stage of considering a transfer plea, the Court is unconcerned with the rival allegations on merits. items.title: State can't take ownership of temple properties through gift deed: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that the State government, which is legally entrusted with protecting temple properties, cannot itself take over such properties by way of a gift deed in the name of public interest or administrative convenience [K Ramalingam and Others v. Government of Tamil Nadu and Others]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe made the observation while holding that the transfer of land belonging to the Nagapalayam Mariamman-Ponnachiamman Temple in Tamil Nadu's Erode district to the State government for the construction of a Taluk Office was illegal. The Court observed that the State's responsibility as a custodian of religious properties did not give it the authority to acquire ownership of such properties. " The State, as custodian, cannot unilaterally usurp, nor permit any of its officers to usurp, the property of the religious/charitable institutions it is charged to protect; a transaction that offends this principle, whatever its label or ostensible public purpose, is liable to be struck down, " the Court said. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The dispute concerned 1 acre and 10 cents of land belonging to the temple at Kodumudi village in Erode district. In August 2017, a temporary trustee executed a gift deed transferring the land to the Tamil Nadu government for the construction of a Taluk Office. The transaction was challenged before the Madras High Court, which dismissed the petition in March 2019, holding that the relevant statutory provision did not expressly prohibit gifts of temple property. Devotees subsequently approached the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court found that the land was an inam property granted for the support and maintenance of the deity. Consequently, Section 41 of the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1959, expressly prohibited its transfer by way of gift. The Court clarified that such a gift was void from the outset and could not be validated even through government sanction. " A gift of an inam property dedicated to the support of a deity is, in consequence, void ab initio and no sanction, however solemnly accorded, could have breathed life into it, " the Court stated. The Bench also rejected the contention that a temporary trustee could transfer temple property without restriction. items.title: Legal education goes beyond criminal and constitutional law: CJI Surya Kant at NLSIU convocation
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Saturday said the purpose of legal education extends beyond learning the principles of criminal or constitutional law. The CJI said that law school is a crucible where ideas collide, where convictions are tested, and where the very essence of dialogue is forged. "The purpose of a legal education extends beyond learning the principles of criminal or constitutional law; it rests in the invigorating experience of encountering those who see the world differently than we do," he said. He was speaking as Chancellor at the 34th convocation of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bangalore. Earlier in the address, he spoke about what the legal profession demands. He said lawyers need the courage to defend what is just and the humility to listen to voices that often go unheard. "This intellectual independence also calls for fairness: hearing before judging, distinguishing a person from a position and disagreeing without denying another person’s dignity," he added. The CJI told the graduating students that a relentless pursuit of honesty will cement their professional reputation. There will be times when compromise tempts and others take shortcuts, he said. In those moments, they should let the wisdom gained at NLSIU be their compass. The CJI said graduates were stepping not only into a profession but into a calling, to be guardians of autonomy and servants of the people. "Law will challenge your patience, test your ethics, and call upon the deepest reserves of your courage. But it will also reward you with the singular joy of service– the serene satisfaction of righting a wrong, the pride of defending liberty, and the honour of upholding the Constitution," he added. He also remembered Urvashi Krishnatra, an LL.B. graduate at the university who has passed away. He said she should have been present to receive her degree and offered condolences to her family and friends on behalf of all present. He thanked the parents for their sacrifice and belief, and praised the faculty and staff for challenging, supporting and inspiring the students. He ended by saying the nation looks to the graduates as "heralds of hope." items.title: Children too have fundamental right to access internet; can't deny it citing online harm: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that children have a fundamental right to access and use the internet and protecting them from online harm cannot justify denying them access altogether [Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr. v. S. Harish & Ors.]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran passed the order while issuing extensive directions to detect and remove child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) online. The Court said that internet access, as a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution, is available to children as well as adults. “We have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing. The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. Our children are entitled to both, ” the Court said in its order passed on 15 October. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran Supreme Court The right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21. Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights. The Court reasoned that measures intended to protect children must target harmful material and those responsible for it, rather than children themselves. In cases involving CSEAM, the wrongdoers are those who create, circulate, sell or seek out such material, and intermediaries that fail to detect and remove it, the Bench said. “ To keep the child away from the internet on account of such failures would be to mistake the victim for the problem, ” it added. However, the Court went on to clarify that its opposition to blanket restrictions on children’s access to the internet did not rule out proportionate safeguards, including parental oversight, a dedicated child mode for social media accounts and restrictions on content inherently harmful to children. items.title: Court sentences Tahir Hussain to 2 years in jail for abetment in Delhi riots case
items.summary: A Delhi court on Friday sentenced former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) councillor Tahir Hussain to two years' imprisonment after convicting him of abetment to rioting in a case related to 2020 Delhi riots. Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh of the Karkardooma Court also imposed a cost of ₹10,000 on Hussain, who is already serving life imprisonment in the Ankit Sharma murder case. "The act attributed to the convict, and for which he stands convicted, is that of providing his house to the rioters for their use. The mere fact that the prosecution did not prove the active participation of the convict in the riot, does not dilute the gravity of his conduct, for the hand that guides is as guilty, if not more, as the hand that acts," the Court said. The Court had convicted Hussain on October 10, while acquitting all other accused in the case . The FIR in the case was registered under Sections 147, 148, 149, 427, 436, 120B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) at Dayalpur police station. One Irshad Ali had filed the complaint alleging that his shop was looted and set on fire on February 24, 2020, causing losses of ₹17–18 lakh in stolen goods and ₹10 lakh in property damage. Another complainant, Mohd Zahid, said rioters raised slogans in support of Tahir Hussain, whom two constables identified during the investigation. Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) Madhukar Pandey appeared for the State. Tahir Hussain was represented through advocate Rajiv Mohan. items.summary: A bench of Supreme Court Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan on Friday quipped that they would sit on a protest ( dharna ) at the main gate of the Delhi High Court if concrete measures are not taken to ensure pedestrian safety on Mathura Road before November 25. The bench expressed dissatisfaction over delays in fixing the dangerous pedestrian crossing near the Delhi High Court junction and the National Zoological Park, where thousands of lawyers, litigants, and children cross daily. While addressing Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Vikramjit Banerjee , said, the Court, in a lighter vein, said, "If you don't do it before the next date, both of us will be at the main gate of the Delhi High Court, and we will not go home until you complete the work. Banerjee responded that a committee was actively looking into the issue after discussions at the highest levels. However, the Court questioned the bureaucratic delay in fixing a basic traffic bottleneck. "Why do you need a committee for this? You need some engineers? "But it has to be completed before 25th November. That’s for sure. No solution. Concrete work to be completed. Otherwise your Chief Secretary will be here beside you. Understood?" the Bench warned. ASG Vikramjit Banerjee Supreme Court If you don't do it before the next date, both of us will be at the main gate of the Delhi High Court, and we will not go home until you complete the work. In October 2025 and September 2026, the Court had flagged the absence of functional red lights, foot overbridges, or traffic-calming measures on the high-density Mathura road stretch. Although a pedestrian signal was installed following court orders, amicus curiae Gaurav Agrawal informed the bench that it frequently remains non-functional, necessitating synchronized signals and speed-limiting rumble strips. The matter will now be heard on November 25. The Court's remarks – even though on the lighter side, come at a time when the national capital has been witnessing a flurry of street protests.

items.title: Supreme Court pulls up Centre over "unannounced" motor accident victim compensation scheme
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed disapproval over the Central government’s quiet rollout of a critical welfare measure for motor accident victims, terming the newly framed Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026 an "unannounced law." A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan observed that beneficial social legislation is rendered meaningless if the general public remains completely unaware of its existence. “This is an unannounced law. People should know because it’s a beneficial piece of legislation. Common man would not come to know,” the Bench remarked, directing the Union government to launch a widespread publicity campaign to inform citizens of their rights under the new rules. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice KV Viswanathan The issue arose during a contempt petition alleging non-compliance with an April 28, 2025 order. The Court had previously directed the Centre to establish a statutory mechanism under Section 164A of the Motor Vehicles Act to ensure swift interim financial relief to road accident victims and their families. During today's hearing, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Vikramjit Banerjee informed the Court that the Central government had indeed framed the scheme, titled the Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026 . Drawing attention to Clause 6, the ASG submitted that a letter had already been dispatched on February 23 to Chief Secretaries of all States to circulate the new guidelines. However, the revelation caught both the applicant (appearing in person) and the amicus curiae entirely by surprise, as neither had any prior knowledge that the scheme had already been framed and dispatched. Beyond the lack of publicity, the amicus curiae and the applicant also flagged that the new scheme applies exclusively to insured motor vehicles where the insurance company disburses compensation. They pointed out that the scheme leaves victims of uninsured motor vehicles unprotected, where the driver or owner of the vehicle is directly liable to pay damages. items.title: Supreme Court stays demolition of CSI church in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday stayed a Madras High Court order directing the demolition of a Christian CSI church at Thippanampatti village of Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi district [ Tirunelveli Diocesan Trust Association v. The District Collector ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath , R Mahadevan , and Aparesh Kumar Singh also sought the response of the Tamil Nadu government and other respondents on a Special Leave Petition (SLP) challenging the High Court's October 1 judgment. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh The case concerned a building that has been used for prayer services by members of the Church of South India (CSI) in Thippanampatti village since 2016. Earlier, a church built around 1972 was being used for prayer services. However, since the old church was too small to accommodate all church-going members, a decision was taken to shift to a new church. In 2014, a CSI Trust purchased 10 cents of land and got permission to use the property to build a CSI community hall. In 2016, a church spire was added to the building and the premises began to be used as a church. However, in June 2016, a local resident named Balakrishna Prabhu moved a plea before the Madras High Court urging it to direct the District Collector to consider his representation seeking a restraint on the construction and operation of the building as a church. items.title: Delhi High Court refuses to stay probe against journalists in SC/ST Act case filed by ACP Vivek Bhagat
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to stay the investigation into the criminal case filed against a woman journalist for allegedly making casteist remarks against Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat during a protest in the national capital on October 3. A request to stay the investigation was made before Justice Mini Pushkarna during the hearing of a plea moved by the journalist for quashing the FIR. Senior Advocate Tanveer Ahmed Mir appearing for the journalist and one other accused requested for an order restraining the police from taking further steps in relation to the investigation in this case. He said that ACP Bhagat's SC/ST Act case was a counterblast to a sexual harassment complaint filed by the woman journalist against him. "I cannot pass such an order [staying investigation]," Justice Pushkarna said. The Court said the case will be heard immediately after the Dussehra break. Justice Mini Pushkarna The Delhi Police had registered the FIR against the woman journalist and one Gajendra Singh, associated with a news portal, as well as an unidentified person, on a complaint filed by ACP Bhagat over alleged casteist remarks during a protest in Delhi on October 3. According to reports, the FIR was registered at Parliament Street police station on October 13 under provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Sections 221, 356(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Bhagat alleged that the journalist made derogatory remarks about his caste and questioned his appointment as an ACP while he was performing law-and-order duties near Jantar Mantar. The case comes amid a separate complaint by the journalist accusing Bhagat of sexual harassment and manhandling during the same protest. On Thursday, the Supreme Court restrained the Delhi Police from taking any coercive action against the journalist in the case registered under the provisions of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. items.title: Lucio AI launches Legal Research Agent in Open Beta, offers 25 Free Searches
items.summary: Lucio AI has launched Lucio Research , a legal research agent released as an open beta through Lucio Labs. The tool searches, screens, reads and cites across hundreds of legal sources for each question. It is free to use for one month, with up to 25 searches per user. The launch addresses a familiar constraint in legal research. Much of the time spent on a research question goes into finding and screening material rather than analysing it and research usually ends when time runs out rather than when every relevant authority has been read. Lucio says the beta is designed to test how far that limit can be pushed. Lucio Research runs in two modes. According to the company, Standard mode runs a focused search of the core authorities and typically reviews 300 to 500 sources per question. In-depth mode explores about three times as many sources and checks for gaps, usually returning an answer in under three minutes. The company says it often reviews 800 to 1,500 sources in this mode and more than 2,000 on some questions. Lucio says that, in its testing, public AI models usually review far fewer sources and that a deep research query on ChatGPT takes around 10 minutes. Each answer cites its authorities inline. A separate view lists every source the tool considered, sorted into highly relevant, relevant, flagged and discarded, so a lawyer can see what was set aside as well as what was relied on. Lucio attributes the speed to its architecture rather than to reading less. In place of a pure agent loop, in which a model takes one step at a time, the system uses fast decision models and an architecture built to maximise parallel work. The company says the tool is optimised for case law research across the US, the UK and India and that its analysis of regulation and legislation is still being improved. Vasu Aggarwal , Co-Founder, Lucio AI, said "Legal research has always been limited by how much a lawyer can read before time runs out. With Lucio Research, we wanted to see how far that limit could move. The citations matter as much as the speed. items.summary: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has sought the Central government's response to a plea challenging the environmental clearance granted for a ₹17,700 crore data centre project being developed as part of Google and Adani Group's artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure initiative in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. [Boddu Reddy v. Union of India] A coram of Judicial Member Justice (retired) Pushpa Sathyanarayana and Expert Member Prashant Gargava posted the matter for further hearing on October 26. The appeal, filed by former Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation corporator Boddu Ganga Rao, challenges the environmental clearance granted on June 10, 2026, to Vizag Hyperscale Data Centre Park Limited, a special purpose vehicle of Adani Infra (India) Limited. The proposed 512 MW data centre at Adavivaram and Mudasarlova villages forms part of Google's larger $15 billion AI hub in Visakhapatnam, being developed in partnership with AdaniConneX and Airtel. The appeal also raises concerns about the project's potential impact on the Mudasarlova Reservoir, an important drinking water source for Visakhapatnam. It claims that the project site lies immediately uphill from the reservoir and that excavation and construction activities could obstruct seven natural streams feeding it. The appellant has argued that despite these concerns, the environmental clearance was granted without an independent hydrological or catchment assessment. The appellant has further questioned a May 8 permission issued by the divisional forest officer for clearing forest growth over 160 acres adjoining the reservoir, alleging that mandatory approvals under forest conservation laws were not obtained. items.title: Calcutta High Court stays order allowing CPI(M) to set up book stall near its office
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Friday stayed a single-judge's order allowing erection of a temporary book stall by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] near its party office at the Bongaon Jessore Road. A bench of Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge and Justice Shabbar Rashidi passed the order on an appeal by the State government. The government had challenged the order passed by Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya on Thursday on a petition moved by the CPI(M). The party had alleged that the State was preventing from installing the stall Advocate Samim Ahammed, representing the CPI(M) pointed out that many people had erected their stalls in the same locality but it was only the CPI(M) members who were being obstructed. He further said that many of these stalls were being operated without proper approval. To this, the Chief Justice said, "Can there be any justification?...Just because many thieves are roaming around, I [CPI(M)] will not be caught?" CPI(M) also said that it is their fundamental duty to disseminate knowledge and information through literature and books. Additional Advocate General Billwadal Bhattacharyya , appearing for the State, said that the CPI(M) members were encroaching public land by erecting their stall and could not prefer a petition to uphold their fundamental rights in the case. He said that the CPI(M) members had suppressed certain documents before the single-judge. "It is the responsibility of police officials to prevent public nuisance," the State counsel said. Considering the arguments, the division bench stayed the operation of the CPI(M) book stall during the remaining Durga Puja days. Meanwhile, the Court took note of a statement that a group namely Hindu Jagran Manch (HJM) has erected their own stall in the place where the CPI(M) book stall was to be set up. The Court directed the State to check whether they have any approval for it and take appropriate steps in case of any violation. The matter will be heard next on January 21, 2027. Additional Advocate General Billwadal Bhattacharyya and advocates Anindya Basu, Arkaprava Sen, Pratip Mukherjee, Srijib Chakraborty, Bikash Kumar Sriwastav and Tamoghna Pramanick represented the State. items.title: Veeramani POCSO case: விசாரணை வளையத்தில் Arun IPS! | CM Vijay | Shabbir Ahmed | TNM Tamil
items.summary: The investigation into the POCSO cases against businessman R Veeramani has widened, and is raising serious questions now about how the Chennai police handled complaints against him. While the SIT continues to share details about private individuals arrested in the case, the Chennai police appear reluctant to disclose details of the inquiry involving its own officers. With no detailed public statement on the questioning of former Chennai Police Commissioner A Arun and former Additional Commissioner (South) N Kannan, questions remain over the transparency of the probe into the police department’s handling of the case. In this week's episode of Yen Endra Kelvi, Shabbir Ahmed examines the latest developments in the Veeramani POCSO case, the questions surrounding the police investigation, and the need for accountability when allegations of serious crimes involve those entitled to enforce the law.

items.summary: Imagine you are on your way to a protest. You haven't reached the protest site. You haven't broken any law. In fact, you haven't even joined the gathering. And yet, the police stop you. Maybe at the airport, outside your home, or on your way there. They put you in a vehicle. And hours later, they let you go. That is what happened to people in New Delhi in the crackdown on protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. And it wasn't just protesters. Journalists covering the protests were detained. Lawyers trying to reach people in custody were stopped. Phones and cameras were seized. People were taken away from the protest site, and in some cases, before they even got there. The Delhi Police say they were maintaining law and order. But there is a fundamental question here: How much power does the police have to stop a protest before it even begins? And when does preventive policing become a way of preventing dissent? items.title: Kochi Mundamveli GCDA-LIFE Mission flats unsafe, amicus curiae tells Kerala HC
items.summary: Residents of the GCDA-LIFE Mission apartment complex in Kochi’s Mundamveli should be urgently moved to safe and habitable accommodation, a court-appointed amicus curiae has told the Kerala High Court. The report flagged sewage leaks, water seepage, corrosion, and other safety concerns at the complex built under the LIFE Mission housing scheme to rehabilitate residents of the P&T Colony in the city. According to a report by The New Indian Express, the amicus curiae found rainwater entering flats through structural joints and wastewater from bathrooms and kitchens on upper floors leaking into apartments below. Water stains and white deposits were found in bathrooms, kitchens, and bedrooms, while prolonged dampness had caused steel structures and duct sheets to corrode. The report also flagged an overflowing septic tank and concerns about the adequacy of the sewage treatment plant, warning that the unhygienic conditions could pose serious health risks. It noted that the building lacked the required safety clearance from a nearby high-tension power line and that the absence of a lift caused difficulties for residents who were seriously ill. The amicus curiae recommended that the court appoint a committee, assisted by approved experts, to assess the building’s structural stability and determine whether it could be used in the future. The report adds to mounting concerns over the complex, which was built by the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA) at a cost of Rs 14.62 crore to rehabilitate families from the flood-prone P&T Colony. Residents moved into the apartments in January 2024 but began reporting leaks and construction defects soon afterwards. The state government is considering a special rehabilitation package for the affected families, Local Self-Governments Minister KM Shaji told the Assembly on October 16. Responding to a calling attention motion by MLA Mohammed Shiyas, he said the government would also pursue an investigation into construction defects and alleged corruption. Shaji said the government had ordered a Vigilance investigation and initiated a preliminary inquiry into alleged irregularities. He added that the Thrissur District Labour Contract Cooperative Society, which carried out the construction, had been terminated after failing to undertake repairs despite repeated instructions. items.title: Eardrum damaged after assault: Kerala activist recounts Delhi Police violence
items.summary: Fidal Royas, a Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) member from Kerala, said he was detained by the Delhi Police five times between October 2 and October 11. On each day, after they were released from detention, Fidal and his comrades would go back to the Communist Party of India (Marxist) head office in HKS Surjeet Bhavan, where they were staying, only to return the next day to the protest site. But on October 11, he was brutally assaulted, leading to a ‘traumatic perforation’ of his eardrum. A native of Kuttiyadi in Kozhikode district, Fidal was among 30-odd DYFI and Students Federation of India (SFI) activists from Kerala who travelled to Delhi on October 1, with the aim of participating in the protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Speaking to TNM, he recounted the events of October 11. Left student and youth organisations took out a march from Rajiv Chowk Metro Station towards Janpath that afternoon. “That day, the demonstration was declared suddenly. We went to Rajiv Chowk between 12 noon and 12.30 pm to take part in it.” Fidal said that he was at the rear end of the march when police started detaining protesters from the back. “I was among the first to be detained and taken into a police bus, the kind with cells. Then others were also detained in the bus, which started moving. Some of us started recording videos from within the bus. The police objected to this and started assaulting us,” he recollected. According to Fidal, one of the cops in the bus stepped out and told five or six others that he had recorded videos. “The cops then proceeded to assault me severely. They put me on the road and beat me with bare hands and kicked me with their boots as I lay on the road. They repeatedly assaulted me, even slapping me on my face till my body couldn’t take it anymore. One after the other, they kept beating me.” “I was beaten continuously for at least five minutes,” Fidal continued, adding that his ear started hurting then. “I was in a lot of pain initially,” he said. The assault continued even after Fidal was put in a second bus, he alleged. “The cops kept assaulting the detainees in that bus also.
